content: 1. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels or effects may be reduced by phenytoin due to its impact on hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Velpatasvir is a substrate of CYP2B6, CYP2C8, and CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative drugs. 2. Moderate-to-potent inducers of CYP2B6, CYP2C8, or CYP3A4 can significantly decrease velpatasvir plasma concentrations, potentially reducing its therapeutic efficacy. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 3. Primidone reduces sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by affecting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter and hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 4. Rabeprazole decreases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by increasing gastric pH, which reduces velpatasvir solubility (practically insoluble at pH > 5). This applies only to oral forms. Avoid co-administration or administer sofosbuvir/velpatasvir with food 4 hours before omeprazole 20 mg. Use with other proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) has not been studied. 5. Rifabutin reduces sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 6. Rifampin decreases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by affecting P-gp efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 7. Rifapentine reduces sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 8. St. John’s Wort decreases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by affecting P-gp efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 9. Sotorasib reduces sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by affecting P-gp efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or refer to prescribing information for dosage adjustments if unavoidable. 10. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases rimegepant levels by affecting P-gp efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 11. Sulbactam levels may increase when co-administered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir due to inhibition of OATP1 transporters. Avoid co-administration or monitor closely. 12. Tepotinib increases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by affecting P-gp efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or reduce the P-gp substrate dosage if recommended. 13. Tipranavir decreases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by affecting P-gp efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 14. Topotecan levels may increase when co-administered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir due to velpatasvir’s inhibition of BCRP transporters. Avoid co-administration or monitor closely. 15. Vinblastine decreases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by affecting P-gp efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 16. Aluminum hydroxide reduces sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by increasing gastric pH, which decreases velpatasvir solubility. Separate administration by at least 4 hours. 17. Calcium carbonate decreases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by increasing gastric pH. Separate administration by at least 4 hours. 18. Atazanavir increases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. 19. Atorvastatin levels may increase when co-administered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir due to velpatasvir’s inhibition of OATP transporters. Monitor closely for myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. 20. Betrixaban levels increase when co-administered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir due to P-gp inhibition. Reduce betrixaban dose to 80 mg once, then 40 mg daily. 21. Cimetidine decreases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer H2 receptor antagonists simultaneously or 12 hours apart at doses not exceeding famotidine 40 mg BID. 22. Clarithromycin increases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. 23. Conivaptan increases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. 24. Danazol increases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. 25. Digoxin levels increase when co-administered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir due to P-gp inhibition. Monitor digoxin levels and adjust dosage as needed. 26. Dipyridamole levels increase when co-administered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir due to velpatasvir’s inhibition of BCRP transporters. Use with caution and monitor closely. 27. Doxorubicin levels increase when co-administered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir due to velpatasvir’s inhibition of BCRP transporters. Use with caution and monitor closely. 28. Elagolix decreases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and consider increasing CYP3A substrate doses if needed. 29. Elbasvir/grazoprevir levels increase when co-administered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir due to velpatasvir’s inhibition of OATP transporters. Use with caution and monitor closely. 30. Eluxadoline levels increase when co-administered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir due to velpatasvir’s inhibition of OATP transporters. Use with caution and monitor closely. 31. Enalapril levels increase when co-administered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir due to velpatasvir’s inhibition of OATP transporters. Use with caution and monitor closely. 32. Everolimus levels increase when co-administered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir due to P-gp inhibition. Monitor closely and adjust dosage as needed. 33. Ezetimibe levels increase when co-administered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir due to velpatasvir’s inhibition of OATP transporters. Use with caution and monitor closely. 34. Famotidine decreases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer H2 receptor antagonists simultaneously or 12 hours apart at doses not exceeding famotidine 40 mg BID. 35. Fexofenadine levels increase when co-administered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir due to velpatasvir’s inhibition of OATP transporters. Use with caution and monitor closely. 36. Fluvastatin levels increase when co-administered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir due to velpatasvir’s inhibition of OATP transporters. Use with caution and monitor closely. 37. Fluvoxamine increases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by affecting CYP2B6 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. 38. Glyburide levels increase when co-administered with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir due to velpatasvir’s inhibition of BCRP transporters. Use with caution and monitor closely. 39. Ibuprofen/famotidine decreases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by increasing gastric pH. Separate administration by at least 4 hours.
